result.title: Weight-Space Programming of Policies and Their Verification via Model Checking
result.summary: Large language models (LLMs) can write the weights of small neural networks directly, without gradient descent. This weight-space programming creates policies for sequential decision-making from a task description alone, but nothing guarantees that a written policy behaves as intended. We combine weight-space programming with probabilistic model checking. Given an environment modeled as a Markov decision process and a requirement in probabilistic computation tree logic (PCTL), an LLM writes all weights of a policy network, optionally repairs them on a dataset of optimal actions, and receives model-checking feedback until the requirement holds or a round limit is reached. The model checker Storm computes, rather than estimates from simulations, the probability that the policy satisfies the requirement, so every returned policy is verified. With two LLMs on three environments, the created policy of each of the 18 runs attains the optimal probability, before any dataset or model-checking feedback. Four of six policies programmed for two transporter jobs also complete three jobs with probability 1, so they generalize to a task that the LLM never saw. The pipeline also programs a policy that satisfies a complex safety requirement expressed with the PCTL until operator in all six runs. In one of them, dataset repair raised the accuracy to 98.4\% but broke the requirement, and one round of model-checking feedback restored it.

AI.brief_summary: 论文让 LLM 不经梯度下降直接写出小型策略网络的权重，并在给定 MDP 环境与 PCTL 需求下调用 Storm 做概率模型检测，用检测反馈迭代修复权重，直到需求满足或达到轮数上限。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「生成—精确验证—修复」闭环与形式化验证反馈，可能为 latent 推理状态是否满足任务约束的核查、停止决策与训练监督提供可核查的思路，但对象是序贯决策策略权重而非多模态推理状态，迁移性需阅读后判断。
